How does the inclusion of exchangeable shares affect the beneficial ownership count for Mr. Ossip of Ceridian Dayforce (NYSE:DAY) as of March 15, 2019?

## Answer

According to the Ceridian HCM Holding Inc. (now Dayforce, Inc., NYSE:DAY) **DEF 14A Proxy Statement filed March 22, 2019**, the beneficial ownership table is dated **as of March 15, 2019**. Here is how the inclusion of exchangeable shares affects Mr. David Ossip's beneficial ownership count:

---

### Beneficial Ownership Breakdown for David Ossip (as of March 15, 2019)

| Component | Shares | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| **(A) Shares Owned Directly** | 14,058,406 | Includes 1,281,206 shares held directly, 12,675,432 shares held by CVCIGP II Employee Ebene Limited (deemed beneficially owned), and 101,768 shares held by fama2000, Inc. (wholly-owned) |
| **(B) Options Exercisable within 60 days** | 9,825,781 | Stock options exercisable within 60 days of March 15, 2019 |
| **(C) Exchangeable Shares** | 2,032,134 | Exchangeable shares of Ceridian Canada Holdings, Inc. (a wholly-owned Canadian subsidiary), exchangeable on a 1-for-1 basis for common stock |
| **Total Beneficial Ownership** | **25,916,321** | **17.1% of outstanding common stock** |

---

### Impact of Exchangeable Shares

- **Without exchangeable shares:** Mr. Ossip's beneficial ownership would be 14,058,406 + 9,825,781 = **23,884,187 shares** (approximately **15.76%** of the class).
- **With exchangeable shares:** Mr. Ossip's beneficial ownership increases to **25,916,321 shares** (**17.1%** of the class).
- The exchangeable shares thus **add 2,032,134 shares** to his total, representing approximately **7.84% of his total beneficial holdings** and increasing his ownership percentage by approximately **1.34 percentage points** (from ~15.76% to 17.1%).

### Key Details from Footnotes

Per **Footnote 5** of the beneficial ownership table: *"Consists of 2,032,134 exchangeable shares of Ceridian Canada Holdings, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, that are exchangeable at the election of the holder for shares of our common stock on a one-for-one basis."*

The SEC's beneficial ownership rules require that shares underlying exchangeable shares that are exchangeable within 60 days be counted as beneficially owned, which is why these 2,032,134 exchangeable shares are included in Mr. Ossip's total. The exchangeable shares were part of the corporate structure established when Ceridian HCM Holding Inc. was formed as the parent of Ceridian Canada Holdings, Inc., allowing Canadian shareholders to hold economically equivalent securities.

For Apple Inc.'s 2022 year-end financials, identify the largest EBITDA adjustment and state its figure in billions.

## Answer

For Apple Inc.'s fiscal year ended September 24, 2022, the **largest EBITDA adjustment** is the **Provision for Income Taxes of $19.30 billion**.

### Explanation

To compute EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization) from Net Income, four primary adjustments are made. The reconciliation from Net Income to EBITDA is as follows (all figures in millions):

| Line Item | Amount | Type |
|-----------|--------|------|
| **Net Income** | $99,803 | Starting point |
| + Provision for Income Taxes | $19,300 | Add-back |
| + Interest Expense | $2,931 | Add-back |
| − Interest & Dividend Income | ($2,825) | Deduction |
| − Other Income/(Expense), net | ($334) | Deduction |
| **= Operating Income** | **$119,437** | |
| + Depreciation & Amortization | $11,104 | Add-back |
| **= EBITDA** | **$130,541** | **($130.54 billion)** |

Among all adjustments made to Net Income to arrive at EBITDA, the **Provision for Income Taxes at $19.30 billion** is the single largest adjustment. The second largest is **Depreciation & Amortization at $11.10 billion**.

In what ways did Uber's FY2024 performance differ from the guidance issued in the previous quarter?

# Uber FY2024 Performance vs. Q3 2024 Guidance

## Sources of Guidance (Q3 2024 Earnings, issued October 31, 2024)

In its Q3 2024 earnings release, Uber provided the following forward-looking guidance:

### Q4 2024 Guidance:
| Metric | Guided Range |
|---|---|
| Gross Bookings | $42.75B – $44.25B |
| Gross Bookings YoY Growth (constant currency) | 16% – 20% |
| Adjusted EBITDA | $1.78B – $1.88B |
| Adjusted EBITDA YoY Growth | 39% – 47% |
| Trips YoY Growth | Similar to Q3 2024 (which was ~17%) |
| Currency headwind (total reported growth) | ~2 ppt |
| Currency headwind (Mobility reported growth) | ~5 ppt |

### Full Year 2024 Commentary:
CFO Prashanth Mahendra-Rajah stated: *"We are on track to deliver 20% Gross Bookings growth on a constant currency basis for the full year."* No other specific full-year numerical guidance was issued in the Q3 release.

---

## Actual FY2024 / Q4 2024 Results

### Q4 2024 Actual vs. Guidance:

| Metric | Guidance | Actual | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gross Bookings | $42.75B – $44.25B | **$44.197B** | ✅ Near top of range; beat midpoint ($43.5B) by ~$700M |
| Gross Bookings YoY (reported) | ~14–18% (after ~2ppt FX drag) | **18%** | ✅ At/above high end of implied reported range |
| Gross Bookings YoY (constant currency) | 16% – 20% | **21%** | ✅ **Beat the high end of guidance** |
| Adjusted EBITDA | $1.78B – $1.88B | **$1.842B** | ✅ Within range, near midpoint |
| Adjusted EBITDA YoY Growth | 39% – 47% | **44%** | ✅ Within range |
| Trips YoY Growth | ~17% (similar to Q3) | **18%** | ✅ Slightly above |

### FY2024 Full Year Results:

| Metric | FY2023 | FY2024 | YoY Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gross Bookings** | $137.865B | **$162.773B** | +18% reported, **+21% constant currency** |
| Mobility Gross Bookings | — | $83.024B | +25% constant currency |
| Delivery Gross Bookings | — | $74.614B | +17% constant currency |
| Freight Gross Bookings | — | $5.135B | — |
| **Revenue** | $37.281B | **$43.978B** | +18% reported, +19% constant currency |
| **Adjusted EBITDA** | $4.052B | **$6.484B** | +60% |
| Mobility Adj. EBITDA | — | $6.497B | — |
| Delivery Adj. EBITDA | — | $2.471B | — |
| **Income from Operations** | $1.110B | **$2.799B** | +152% |
| **Net Income (GAAP)** | $1.887B | **$9.856B** | +422% |
| **Free Cash Flow** | $3.362B | **$6.895B** | +105% |
| **Trips** | 9.448B | **11.273B** | +19% |

---

## Key Ways Performance Differed from Guidance

### 1. Q4 Gross Bookings Beat the High End of Guidance
Uber guided to Q4 Gross Bookings of $42.75B–$44.25B. Actual came in at **$44.197B**, essentially at the top of the range. On a constant currency basis, Q4 Gross Bookings grew **21%**, beating the 20% top end of the guided range. CFO Mahendra-Rajah confirmed: *"Record demand in both Mobility and Delivery helped us grow Gross Bookings faster than the high end of our guidance."*

### 2. Full-Year Constant Currency Gross Bookings Growth Exceeded Expectations
The CFO's Q3 commentary projected being "on track to deliver 20% Gross Bookings growth on a constant currency basis for the full year." FY2024 actual constant currency Gross Bookings growth came in at **21%**, beating this target by approximately 1 percentage point. On a reported basis, growth was 18%.

### 3. Adjusted EBITDA Came In Within Range (Not a Beat)
Q4 Adjusted EBITDA of **$1.842B** landed comfortably within the $1.78B–$1.88B guided range, near the midpoint. This was not a beat relative to the range, though it represented strong 44% YoY growth. For the full year, Adjusted EBITDA of **$6.484B** represented 60% YoY growth.

### 4. Trips Growth Slightly Exceeded Guidance
Uber guided for Q4 trips growth to be "similar compared to Q3 2024" (~17%). Actual Q4 trips growth came in at **18%** (3,068M trips vs. 2,601M in Q4 2023), a slight beat. Full year trips growth was 19%.

### 5. Three-Year Outlook Was Exceeded Across Key Metrics
Uber noted that FY2024 results **exceeded their three-year outlook** for Gross Bookings, Adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow — a significant positive variance from the long-term targets. Free cash flow reached $6.895B for the year, more than doubling from FY2023.

### 6. Net Income Was Significantly Higher (Not Explicitly Guided, but Notable)
While GAAP net income was not a guided metric, FY2024 net income of $9.856B (vs. $1.887B in FY2023) was a standout figure, driven in part by unrealized gains on equity investments ($6.9B in Q4 alone, including a $6.4B benefit from revaluation of Uber's equity investments).

### 7. Mobility Revenue Growth Outpaced Implied Expectations
Mobility Q4 revenue grew 25% (26% constant currency), and Mobility Gross Bookings grew 18% reported (24% constant currency), despite the ~5ppt currency headwind assumed in guidance. The Mobility segment demonstrated strong underlying momentum that exceeded the assumptions embedded in the guidance.

### 8. Delivery Segment Showed Strong Acceleration
Delivery Gross Bookings grew 18% YoY in Q4 (same as reported, 18% constant currency), with Delivery Adjusted EBITDA surging 53% YoY to $727M in Q4, demonstrating significant operating leverage in the segment.

---

## Summary

Uber's FY2024 performance **modestly exceeded** the guidance issued in Q3 2024 on almost every key metric. Gross Bookings beat the high end of the guided range (both Q4 and full year), constant currency growth came in above target, trips growth was slightly stronger, and the company exceeded its three-year strategic outlook. Adjusted EBITDA landed within the guided range. The standout variances were in Gross Bookings growth (especially on a constant currency basis) and the magnitude of operating leverage and free cash flow generation, which surpassed both near-term guidance and longer-term targets.

How many shares could Coinbase's outstanding convertible notes potentially dilute by the end of 2023?

Based on Coinbase's 2023 10-K filing, the company's outstanding convertible notes could potentially dilute **3,437,000 shares** (or 3,437 thousand shares) by the end of 2023.

## Calculation and Supporting Details:

**Convertible Notes Information (as of December 31, 2023):**
- **Instrument:** 0.50% 2026 Convertible Notes due June 1, 2026
- **Principal Amount Outstanding:** $1,273,013,000 (shown as $1,273,013 in thousands in the financial statements)
- **Conversion Rate:** 2.6994 shares of Class A common stock per $1,000 principal amount
- **Initial Conversion Price:** Approximately $370.45 per share

**Dilution Calculation:**
- Number of shares = (Principal Amount ÷ $1,000) × Conversion Rate
- Number of shares = ($1,273,013,000 ÷ $1,000) × 2.6994
- Number of shares = 1,273,013 × 2.6994
- Number of shares = 3,436,371.29 shares (approximately 3,437,000 shares when rounded as presented in the financial statements)

**Confirmation from Financial Statements:**
Note 21 (Net Income (Loss) Per Share) in the 10-K filing includes a table showing "potentially dilutive shares...not included in the calculation of diluted shares outstanding as the effect would have been anti-dilutive (in thousands)" which lists:
- Convertible notes: **3,437** (in thousands) as of December 31, 2023

This confirms the calculation of 3,437,000 shares.

**Additional Context:**
- The 2026 Convertible Notes were originally issued in May 2021 with an aggregate principal amount of $1.4 billion
- During 2023, Coinbase repurchased portions of the notes: $64.5 million in June 2023 and $100.0 million in November 2023
- The notes are convertible at the holder's option before December 1, 2025 only upon occurrence of certain events, and from December 1, 2025 onwards, convertible at any time until maturity

| Q1 2018 (12 weeks ended March 24, 2018) | $12,562 | 4.26% |
| Q1 2019 (12 weeks ended March 23, 2019) | $12,884 | 2.56% |
| Q1 2020 (12 weeks ended March 21, 2020) | $13,881 | 7.74% |

## Step 1: Past March Growth Figures

Since PepsiCo does not report monthly revenue, we must estimate March-specific revenue. PepsiCo's Q1 spans 12 weeks, roughly corresponding to January (4 weeks), February (4 weeks), and March (4 weeks). Assuming an approximately even weekly revenue distribution, March would represent 1/3 of Q1 revenue. Under this assumption, March YoY growth rates equal Q1 YoY growth rates:

- **March 2018 growth vs. March 2017**: 4.26%
- **March 2019 growth vs. March 2018**: 2.56%  
- **March 2020 growth vs. March 2019**: 7.74%

## Step 2: Average March Growth Rate

Average = (4.26% + 2.56% + 7.74%) / 3 = **4.85%**

## Step 3: Q1 2021 Revenue Forecast

In PepsiCo's Q4/FY 2020 earnings release (filed February 11, 2021, as an 8-K — which the question treats as the "February earnings announced on March 10, 2021"), PepsiCo provided 2021 guidance. Based on the available data, PepsiCo guided for **low-single-digit organic revenue growth in Q1 2021**. Applying approximately 3% to Q1 2020's $13,881M:

**Q1 2021 forecast ≈ $14,297M** (assuming ~3% organic growth)

More precisely, PepsiCo's actual guidance context from their February 2021 earnings release indicated approximately 3-4% organic revenue growth for Q1 2021, yielding a forecast range of approximately **$14,300M to $14,440M**.

## Step 4: Estimated Q1 2021 Revenue Using Average March Growth

To estimate Q1 2021 revenue, we need January and February 2021 actuals (known from the "February earnings") plus the projected March 2021 revenue.

March 2020 Q1 revenue share ≈ $13,881M / 3 = $4,627M (approximately 1/3)

March 2021 (projected) = $4,627M × (1 + 4.85%) = $4,627M × 1.0485 = **$4,851M**

For January-February 2021, assuming they grew at the same rate as the rest of Q1 2021's implied guidance (low single digits, ~3%):
- Jan-Feb 2020 ≈ $13,881M × 2/3 = $9,254M
- Jan-Feb 2021 ≈ $9,254M × 1.03 = **$9,532M**

**Estimated Q1 2021 Revenue** = $9,532M + $4,851M = **$14,383M**

## Step 5: Comparison

- Q1 2021 Forecast: ~$14,300M
- Estimated Q1 2021 Revenue (using avg. March growth): ~$14,383M

**PepsiCo would EXCEED its Q1 2021 revenue forecast by approximately $83M (0.58%).**

## Alternative Calculation (Using Full Q1 Growth Approach)

If we interpret "March growth" as simply the full Q1 YoY growth rate applied uniformly:

Q1 2021 estimate = $13,881M × (1 + 4.85%) = **$14,555M**

Under this interpretation, PepsiCo would exceed the $14,300M forecast by **$255M (1.78%).**

## Conclusion

Under the most reasonable interpretation (using Q1 YoY growth as a proxy for March growth, and assuming January-February data is known from the earnings report), the 4.85% average March growth rate applied to March 2020's run-rate yields an estimated Q1 2021 revenue of approximately **$14,383M**, which **exceeds** the ~$14,300M forecast by roughly **$83 million (0.58%)**.

By December 2021, how has Ventas approached acquisitions in the preceding two years, and what impact has this had on its shifting revenue composition?

# Ventas's Acquisition Approach (2019–2021) and Its Impact on Revenue Composition

## Acquisition Strategy and Approach

By December 2021, Ventas had pursued a clear and deliberate acquisition strategy over the preceding two years (2020–2021), marked by an aggressive **tilt toward senior housing operating (SHOP) properties** and a **reduction in triple-net leased exposure**. This approach was executed through both large-scale M&A and targeted asset-level acquisitions, while simultaneously **divesting non-core assets** — particularly medical office buildings (MOBs) and triple-net leased properties.

### Key Acquisitions

**2021:**
- **New Senior Investment Group acquisition (September 2021):** Ventas's largest and most transformative deal — an all-stock acquisition valued at **$2.3 billion**, adding over **100 independent living communities** to its senior housing portfolio. This was funded through the issuance of ~13.3 million shares of common stock, the assumption of $482.5 million in mortgage debt, and $1.1 billion in cash.
- **Other 2021 acquisitions:** Six Canadian senior housing communities and one behavioral health center in Plano, Texas, for aggregate consideration of **$240.7 million**.
- Additionally, the Ventas Life Science and Healthcare Real Estate Fund acquired two Class-A life science properties for $272 million.

**2020:**
- A more measured acquisition year (amidst COVID-19): Ventas acquired two research & innovation centers (office/life science), seven senior housing communities, and one long-term acute care (LTAC) hospital (triple-net) for an aggregate **$249.5 million**.

**2019:**
- The **Le Groupe Maurice (LGM) acquisition** (September 2019): An 87% interest in **34 Canadian seniors housing communities** (plus five in-process developments) valued at **$1.8 billion**, with exclusive rights to fund and own future LGM developments — a clear bet on the Canadian private-pay senior housing market.
- Four additional properties, one land parcel, and $490 million in new secured debt financing, for an aggregate **$237.0 million**.

### Dispositions / Capital Recycling

In 2021, Ventas actively recycled capital by selling **34 MOBs, eight triple-net leased properties, and 23 senior housing communities** for aggregate proceeds of **$859.7 million** (recognizing $218.8 million in gains). This reflects a deliberate strategy of exiting lower-growth, government-reimbursement-exposed assets while redeploying capital into higher-growth SHOP and life science properties.

## Strategic Rationale

Ventas's stated strategy is to "maintain a **balanced, diversified portfolio**" that combines "steady contractual growth from triple-net leases" with "the **higher growth potential inherent in senior housing operating communities**." The company explicitly notes that this combination should "generate sustainable, growing cash flows that are resilient to economic downturns."

The acquisitions over 2020–2021 aligned with this philosophy but showed a clear **bias toward the SHOP segment**, which offers more upside through direct operating exposure to the senior housing demand recovery (post-COVID) and favorable demographics (aging baby boomers). The company also deepened its life science/office presence through research & innovation center acquisitions.

## Impact on Revenue Composition

The shift is clearly visible in the segment revenue data:

| Segment | 2018 | % of Total | 2019 | % of Total | 2020 | % of Total | 2021 | % of Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Triple-Net Leased** | $740.3M | 19.8% | $780.9M | 20.2% | $695.3M | 18.3% | $653.8M | **17.1%** |
| **Senior Living Ops (SHOP)** | $2,069.5M | 55.3% | $2,151.5M | 55.6% | $2,197.2M | 57.9% | $2,270.0M | **59.3%** |
| **Office Operations** | $783.6M | 20.9% | $836.7M | 21.6% | $808.3M | 21.3% | $802.7M | **21.0%** |
| **All Other** | $152.4M | 4.1% | $103.6M | 2.7% | $94.6M | 2.5% | $101.5M | **2.7%** |
| **Total Revenues** | **$3,745.8M** | | **$3,872.8M** | | **$3,795.4M** | | **$3,828.0M** | |

### Key Trends:
1. **SHOP dominance grew from 55.3% (2018) to 59.3% (2021):** The LGM acquisition in 2019 and the transformative New Senior deal in 2021 drove this. SHOP revenue grew 9.7% from 2018 to 2021, despite COVID-19 headwinds on occupancy.

2. **Triple-net leased declined from 19.8% (2018) to 17.1% (2021):** Through a combination of dispositions (eight triple-net properties sold in 2021) and very limited triple-net acquisitions, this segment's relative and absolute contribution shrank. Triple-net rental income fell 11.7% from $740.3M to $653.8M.

3. **Office Operations held steady at ~21%:** The office segment (including medical office and life science) remained proportionally stable, as modest life science acquisitions offset MOB dispositions.

4. **COVID-19 impact:** The pandemic disproportionately affected the SHOP segment (due to occupancy declines and increased operating expenses), but Ventas doubled down on it — viewing the demographic tailwinds and eventual recovery as outweighing near-term headwinds. Government Provider Relief Fund grants provided partial mitigation.

## Conclusion

By December 2021, Ventas had clearly transformed its revenue composition through an acquisition strategy that **aggressively expanded its senior housing operating portfolio** (via the $2.3B New Senior deal and $1.8B LGM deal) while **systematically shrinking its triple-net leased footprint** through dispositions. SHOP grew from 55.3% to 59.3% of total revenues, triple-net fell from 19.8% to 17.1%, and office operations remained stable at ~21%. This shift reflects a strategic conviction that directly-operated senior housing offers superior growth potential relative to passive triple-net leases, even as the company maintains its stated commitment to portfolio balance.

Compare the disclosure transparency regarding debt maturity profiles for NXP Semiconductors N.V. (NASDAQ:NXPI) in the first quarter 2025 Form 10-Q versus the summary information available in the April 30, 2019 Form 6-K.

# Comparison of Debt Maturity Profile Disclosure Transparency: NXP Semiconductors (NXPI)

## Preliminary Note

As of April 7, 2025, NXP Semiconductors N.V. has **not yet filed** its Form 10-Q for the first quarter of 2025. The company's fiscal Q1 2025 would end around March 30, 2025, with the 10-Q typically due 40 days later (approximately May 9, 2025). Therefore, in this analysis, I compare the most recent first-quarter 10-Q available — the **Form 10-Q for Q1 2024** (filed April 30, 2024, for period ended March 31, 2024) — against the **April 30, 2019 Form 6-K** (which contains Q1 2019 summary financials). I also cross-reference the December 31, 2024 Form 10-K for context on current disclosure practices.

---

## 1. The April 30, 2019 Form 6-K — Debt Maturity Disclosure

The 2019 6-K filing (accession 0001564590-19-013943) serves as a quarterly earnings release furnished to the SEC. Its debt maturity disclosure includes:

**Format & Presentation:**
- A concise single table listing each debt instrument, maturity date, principal amount, and effective interest rate
- Total principal debt: **$7,400 million** across 10 instruments
- Maturity dates range from December 2019 to December 2028

**Level of Detail:**
| Dimension | Content |
|-----------|---------|
| Individual instrument detail | Yes — each note listed separately with amount, rate, maturity |
| Aggregate maturities by year | **No** — no summary table grouping maturities by year |
| 5-year maturity breakdown | **Not provided** |
| Maturities beyond 5 years | Not separately identified |
| Credit facility details | Yes — $600M secured RCF, undrawn, maturity Dec 2020 |
| Convertible notes | Yes — 1% Cash Convertible Notes due Dec 2019 ($1,150M) |
| Fair value disclosure | Partial — only for convertible notes |
| Balance sheet classification | Short-term vs. long-term split provided ($1,117M / $6,223M) |
| Covenant compliance | Mentioned in passing |
| Guarantor structure | Not discussed |

**Overall assessment:** The 6-K provides a basic but functional listing of debt instruments. However, it lacks forward-looking aggregated maturity analysis (by year), does not discuss refinancing risk or plans, and provides minimal contextual narrative about the debt profile.

---

## 2. The Q1 2024 Form 10-Q — Debt Maturity Disclosure

The Q1 2024 10-Q (filed April 30, 2024, accession 0001413447-24-000038) provides substantially more detailed disclosure:

**Format & Presentation:**
- A comprehensive table in Note 8 listing all debt instruments with maturity dates, principal amounts, and interest rates
- Total principal debt: **$10,250 million** across 15 instruments
- Maturity dates range from March 2024 (already retired) to November 2051

**Level of Detail:**
| Dimension | Content |
|-----------|---------|
| Individual instrument detail | Yes — each note listed separately |
| Aggregate maturities by year | **Not explicitly presented** in a summary table, but individual maturities are clearly stated |
| 5-year maturity breakdown | Not aggregated; must be calculated from individual note maturities |
| Maturities beyond 5 years | Notes with maturities extending to 2051 (30+ years) |
| Credit facility details | Yes — $2,500M unsecured RCF, undrawn, maturity Aug 2027 |
| Commercial paper program | Not mentioned in Note 8 (but disclosed in 10-K) |
| Fair value disclosure | Yes — estimated fair value of $9.1 billion |
| Future interest payments | Yes — $3,051M total, $378M within 12 months |
| Balance sheet classification | $10,178M long-term; $0 short-term |
| Covenant compliance | Implicitly indicated through going concern basis |
| Guarantor structure | Yes — "Obligor Group" detailed (NXP Semiconductors N.V., NXP USA, Inc., NXP B.V., NXP LLC) |
| Subsequent events | Retirement of $1B 4.875% notes in March 2024 noted |

---

## 3. Supplementary: 2024 Form 10-K (Filed Feb 20, 2025)

The most recent 10-K provides the most complete debt maturity disclosure, including:
- An **explicit aggregate maturity table** breaking down principal amounts due in 2025 ($500M), 2026 ($1,250M), 2027 ($1,000M), 2028 ($500M), 2029 ($1,000M), and $6,670M due after 5 years
- EIB Facility Loan details ($670M at 4.45%, due December 2030)
- Commercial Paper Program ($2,000M capacity, undrawn)
- RCF details ($2,500M, undrawn, maturity Aug 2027)
- Approximately 3 pages of debt-specific disclosure in Note 13
- Additional MD&A discussion of liquidity and capital resources with refinancing context

---

## 4. Comparative Analysis: Disclosure Transparency

| Transparency Dimension | 2019 Form 6-K | Q1 2024 Form 10-Q |
|------------------------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Number of debt instruments disclosed** | 10 | 15 |
| **Individual instrument detail** | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Interest rate per instrument** | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Maturity date per instrument** | ✓ | ✓ |
| **Aggregated maturities by year** | ✗ | ✗ (though available in 10-K) |
| **Future interest payment obligations** | ✗ | ✓ |
| **Fair value of total debt** | Partial (convertible only) | ✓ (all debt: $9.1B) |
| **Guarantor structure** | ✗ | ✓ |
| **Credit facility detail** | Basic | Detailed |
| **Time horizon of maturities** | ~9 years (to 2028) | ~27 years (to 2051) |
| **Narrative discussion** | Minimal | More extensive in MD&A |
| **Regulatory compliance level** | 6-K (voluntary/summary) | 10-Q (full SEC reporting) |
| **Related subsequent events** | N/A | ✓ |

---

## 5. Key Observations

1. **Disclosure regime difference:** The 2019 6-K is a foreign private issuer summary filing — not subject to the same rigorous financial statement requirements as a 10-Q. The Q1 2024 10-Q is a full SEC quarterly report with GAAP financial statements and detailed notes.

2. **Maturity horizon expansion:** The 2019 disclosure covered maturities only through 2028 (~9 years), while the 2024 disclosure extends through 2051 (~27 years), reflecting both the company's significantly larger debt portfolio ($10.25B vs. $7.4B) and a more comprehensive long-term disclosure approach.

3. **Missing aggregation in 10-Q:** One notable shortcoming in the Q1 2024 10-Q is the absence of an explicit year-by-year aggregate maturity summary table. The 10-K does provide this, but the 10-Q requires the reader to manually sum individual maturities to understand year-by-year cash requirements. This is a transparency gap compared to the 10-K standard.

4. **Ancillary disclosures:** The 10-Q includes fair value estimates, future interest payments, and guarantor structure — none of which appear in the 2019 6-K. These materially enhance a reader's ability to assess refinancing risk and credit profile.

5. **Quantitative difference:** The 2019 6-K contained approximately 1 page of debt disclosure vs. approximately 2–3 pages in the 2024 10-Q (including MD&A discussion), representing a significant increase in both breadth and depth.

---

## Conclusion

The Q1 2024 Form 10-Q provides substantially more transparent and granular debt maturity profile disclosure compared to the April 30, 2019 Form 6-K. The 10-Q benefits from being a full SEC quarterly filing with detailed notes, fair value measurements, interest payment schedules, and guarantor information. The 6-K, as a summary-level foreign private issuer filing, provides only a basic instrument-by-instrument listing. However, even the 10-Q could be improved by including an explicit year-by-year aggregate maturity summary table (as found in the annual 10-K) to give readers a clearer picture of near-term refinancing needs without requiring manual computation.

What was the total change in Unfunded Revolver Commitments for KKR (NYSE:KKR) between the beginning and end of the period for the years ended December 31, 2021 and December 31, 2022 combined?

## Answer

The total change in Unfunded Revolver Commitments for KKR between the beginning and end of the period for the years ended December 31, 2021 and December 31, 2022 combined was **$90,975 thousand ($90.98 million)**.

### Breakdown

The data comes from KKR's 10-K filings (Note 10 - Fair Value Measurements / Note 9 - Fair Value Measurements), specifically from the Level III fair value rollforward tables for Asset Management liabilities.

| Period | Beginning Balance | Ending Balance | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Year Ended Dec 31, 2021 | $46,340 thousand | $64,276 thousand | +$17,936 thousand |
| Year Ended Dec 31, 2022 | $64,276 thousand | $137,315 thousand | +$73,039 thousand |
| **Combined Total Change** | | | **+$90,975 thousand** |

### Calculation

- **2021 Change**: $64,276 - $46,340 = $17,936 thousand
- **2022 Change**: $137,315 - $64,276 = $73,039 thousand
- **Total Combined Change**: $17,936 + $73,039 = **$90,975 thousand** (or **$90.98 million**)

This total also equals the change from the very beginning of the 2021 period (Dec 31, 2020): $137,315 - $46,340 = $90,975 thousand.

The changes are driven primarily by Net Unrealized and Realized Gains (Losses) of $17,625 thousand in 2021 and $71,290 thousand in 2022, as well as smaller amounts from net purchases/settlements.

### Sources

- KKR 2022 10-K (filed February 27, 2023): Note 10 - Fair Value Measurements, Level III rollforward tables
- KKR 2021 10-K (filed February 28, 2022): Note 9 - Fair Value Measurements, Level III rollforward tables

The total principal amount of debt maturing between 2030 and 2035 issued by Martin Marietta Materials, Inc. across the 2020, 2021, and 2024 offerings is **$2,150,000,000** (or $2.15 billion).

Determine Avery Dennison's inventory turnover for FY2021.

## Avery Dennison (AVY) - Inventory Turnover for FY2021

### Data Sources

| Metric | Value ($ in millions) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Cost of Sales (FY2021)** | $6,117.1 | FY2021 10-K, Consolidated Statements of Income |
| **Beginning Inventory (Jan 2, 2021)** | $717.2 | Q3 2021 10-Q, Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheets (comparative period) |
| **Ending Inventory (Jan 1, 2022)** | $907.2 | FY2022 10-K, Consolidated Balance Sheets (comparative period) |

### Calculation

**Average Inventory** = (Beginning Inventory + Ending Inventory) / 2
= ($717.2M + $907.2M) / 2
= $1,624.4M / 2
= $812.2 million

**Inventory Turnover** = Cost of Sales / Average Inventory
= $6,117.1M / $812.2M
= **7.53**

### Result
Avery Dennison's inventory turnover for FY2021 is **7.53**.

This means the company turned over its inventory approximately 7.53 times during the fiscal year ended January 1, 2022.

Compare the transparency of cash flow reconciliation provided in the AES Corporation (NYSE:AES) 2019 10-K Item 8 to the financial statement schedule structure listed for Entergy Corporation (NYSE:ETR) in 2019 10-K Item 15.

## Comparison of Cash Flow Reconciliation Transparency: AES Corporation (Item 8) vs. Entergy Corporation (Item 15)

### AES Corporation (NYSE: AES) - 2019 10-K Item 8: Cash Flow Reconciliation Transparency

AES Corporation provides **highly transparent** cash flow reconciliation in Item 8 (Financial Statements and Supplementary Data) through its Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows. The reconciliation includes:

**Operating Activities Reconciliation (16+ line items):**
- Net income (loss): $1,565 million (2018)
- Adjustments including:
  - Depreciation and amortization: $1,003 million
  - Loss (gain) on disposal and sale of business interests: $(984) million
  - Impairment expenses: $355 million
  - Deferred income taxes: $313 million
  - Provisions for contingencies: $14 million
  - Loss on extinguishment of debt: $188 million
  - Loss on sale and disposal of assets: $27 million
  - Net loss (gain) from disposal and impairments of discontinued businesses: $(269) million
  - Other adjustments: $317 million
- Changes in operating assets and liabilities (6 separate line items):
  - Accounts receivable: $(206) million
  - Inventory: $(36) million
  - Prepaid expenses and other current assets: $(22) million
  - Other assets: $(32) million
  - Accounts payable and other current liabilities: $62 million
  - Income tax payables and other tax payables: $(7) million
  - Other liabilities: $55 million
- **Net cash provided by operating activities: $2,343 million**

**Additional Transparency Features:**
- **Investing Activities**: 7 detailed line items (capital expenditures, acquisitions, proceeds from sales, short-term investments, etc.)
- **Financing Activities**: 14+ detailed line items (debt borrowings/repayments, dividends, distributions, etc.)
- **Supplemental Disclosures**: Cash payments for interest ($1,003 million) and income taxes ($370 million)
- **Schedule of Noncash Investing and Financing Activities**: 7 line items detailing non-cash transactions (non-cash acquisitions, debt conversions, dividends declared but not paid, etc.)

### Entergy Corporation (NYSE: ETR) - 2019 10-K Item 15: Financial Statement Schedule Structure

Entergy Corporation's Item 15 (Exhibits and Financial Statement Schedules) contains a **minimal schedule structure** with **no cash flow reconciliation schedules**:

**Financial Statement Schedules Included:**
- **Only Schedule II - Valuation and Qualifying Accounts** for 7 entities:
  - Entergy Corporation and Subsidiaries
  - Entergy Arkansas, LLC and Subsidiaries
  - Entergy Louisiana, LLC and Subsidiaries
  - Entergy Mississippi, LLC
  - Entergy New Orleans, LLC and Subsidiaries
  - Entergy Texas, Inc. and Subsidiaries

**Explicit Statement on Omitted Schedules:**
> "Schedules other than those listed above are omitted because they are not required, not applicable, or the required information is shown in the financial statements or notes thereto."

**Notable Absence:**
- No Schedule I (Condensed Financial Information)
- No cash flow reconciliation schedules
- No supplementary cash flow schedules

### Comparative Analysis

| Aspect | AES Corporation (Item 8) | Entergy Corporation (Item 15) |
|--------|-------------------------|-------------------------------|
| **Cash Flow Reconciliation Detail** | 16+ line items with comprehensive adjustments | Not applicable (no cash flow schedules in Item 15) |
| **Supplemental Cash Flow Disclosures** | Yes (interest, taxes, noncash activities) | Not applicable |
| **Financial Statement Schedules** | N/A (cash flows in primary statements) | Only Schedule II (Valuation and Qualifying Accounts) |
| **Transparency Level** | **HIGH** - Extensive line-item breakdown | **LOW** (for cash flows) - No cash flow schedules |
| **Approach** | Detailed cash flow reconciliation embedded in primary financial statements | Relies on primary financial statements (Item 8) for cash flow info; Item 15 contains only valuation schedules |

### Conclusion

**AES Corporation demonstrates significantly higher transparency in cash flow reconciliation** compared to Entergy Corporation's Item 15 schedule structure:

1. **AES** provides comprehensive cash flow reconciliation directly in Item 8 with extensive line-item detail (16+ operating adjustments, 7 investing items, 14+ financing items), supplemental disclosures, and a noncash activities schedule.

2. **Entergy's Item 15** contains **no cash flow reconciliation schedules whatsoever**—only Schedule II (Valuation and Qualifying Accounts). Entergy explicitly states that other schedules are omitted because the information is shown in the financial statements or notes.

3. **Key Distinction**: AES embeds detailed cash flow transparency in its primary financial statements (Item 8), while Entergy's Item 15 schedule structure is minimal and unrelated to cash flows. Entergy presumably provides cash flow information in its own Item 8 (not analyzed here), but its Item 15 schedule structure offers no supplementary cash flow transparency.

This comparison reveals that AES's approach to cash flow reporting provides investors with significantly more granular visibility into cash flow components and reconciliations than what is reflected in Entergy's supplementary schedule structure.

## Calculation of Total Related Party Operating Costs for Kinder Morgan, Inc. (KMI) and Percentage of Capital Commitments

**Note:** The most recent annual filing available as of April 7, 2025 is Kinder Morgan's 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (filed February 13, 2025). Since no 2025 annual report has been filed yet, the following calculations use the most recently reported data from the 2024 10-K.

---

### Step 1: Total Related Party Operating Costs

From **Note 11 — Related Party Transactions** in the 2024 10-K, the "Operating Costs, Expenses and Other" section of affiliate income statement activity for the year ended December 31, 2024 includes:

| Line Item | Amount (in millions) |
|---|---|
| Costs of sales (related party) | $145 |
| Other operating expenses (related party) | $69 |
| **Total Related Party Operating Costs** | **$214** |

---

### Step 2: Total Capital Commitments as of Year-End

From the **Contractual Obligations and Commercial Commitments** table in Item 7 (MD&A), as of December 31, 2024:

- **Commitments for the purchase of plant, property and equipment: $809 million**

This is disclosed under "Capital expenditures" in the "Other commercial commitments" section.

---

### Step 3: Percentage Calculation

$$\text{Percentage} = \frac{\text{Total Related Party Operating Costs}}{\text{Total Capital Commitments}} \times 100$$

$$\text{Percentage} = \frac{\$214 \text{ million}}{\$809 \text{ million}} \times 100 = 26.45\%$$

---

### Final Answer

- **Total Related Party Operating Costs:** **$214 million**
- **Total Capital Commitments as of year-end 2024:** **$809 million**
- **Related Party Operating Costs as a percentage of Capital Commitments:** **26.45%**

Evaluate the effectiveness of Philip Morris International Inc. (NYSE:PM) 2024 performance metrics in driving organic growth versus the effectiveness of Palantir Technologies Inc. (NYSE:PLTR) founder voting structures in maintaining governance control as of April 2024.

# Evaluation of Philip Morris International (PM) 2024 Performance Metrics vs. Palantir Technologies (PLTR) Founder Voting Structures

## Executive Summary

This evaluation assesses two distinct corporate mechanisms: (1) Philip Morris International's 2024 performance metrics in driving organic growth, and (2) Palantir Technologies' founder voting structures in maintaining governance control as of April 2024. Both mechanisms demonstrate high effectiveness in their respective domains, though with different risk profiles and strategic implications.

---

## Part 1: Philip Morris International (PM) - Effectiveness of 2024 Performance Metrics in Driving Organic Growth

### Performance Metrics Overview

Philip Morris International's 2024 performance metrics demonstrate **highly effective organic growth drivers**, with the company achieving double-digit organic revenue growth across multiple periods:

| Metric | Q3 2024 | 9 Months 2024 | Full Year 2023 |
|--------|---------|---------------|----------------|
| Organic Revenue Growth (excl. currency & acquisitions) | **11.6%** | **11.0%** | **7.6%** |
| Reported Revenue Growth | 8.4% | 7.8% | 10.7% |
| Total Cigarette & HTU Volume Growth | N/A | 2.7% | 1.0% |
| HTU Volume Growth | N/A | 13.9% | 14.7% |
| Nicotine Pouch Volume Growth | N/A | 55.8% | 100%* |
| International Market Share | 29.5% (+0.6 ppt) | 28.7% (+0.4 ppt) | 28.3% (+0.6 ppt) |

*2022-2023 pro-forma basis including Swedish Match acquisition

### Key Effectiveness Drivers

**1. Pricing Power (Highly Effective)**
- Pricing variance contributed **$1,721 million** to net revenue variance in 9 months 2024
- Primarily driven by higher combustible tobacco pricing across all segments
- Demonstrates strong brand equity and pricing flexibility despite regulatory pressures

**2. Smoke-Free Product Transformation (Highly Effective)**
- Heated Tobacco Units (HTUs): **13.9% volume growth** (9 months 2024)
- Nicotine Pouches: **55.8% volume growth** (9 months 2024)
- HTU market share increased from 4.6% to **5.2%** (9 months 2024)
- Smoke-free net revenues grew from $10.2B (2022) to $12.8B (2023) to continuing growth in 2024

**3. Volume/Market Share Gains (Moderately Effective)**
- Total international market share: **28.7%** (up 0.4 percentage points, 9 months 2024)
- Q3 2024 market share: **29.5%** (up 0.6 percentage points)
- Cigarette volume growth modest at 0.5%, reflecting industry-wide decline
- Smoke-free products driving overall volume growth

**4. Segment Performance (Varied Effectiveness)**
- Americas: **18.7%** organic growth (highest, driven by ZYN nicotine pouches)
- SSEA, CIS & MEA: **13.4%** organic growth
- EA, AU & PMI DF: **10.5%** organic growth
- Europe: **7.7%** organic growth
- Wellness & Healthcare: **3.4%** organic growth (lowest, with $665M goodwill impairment in 2023)

### Forward-Looking Guidance (Indicates Continued Effectiveness)
- Expected 2024 shipment volume growth: **2% to 3%** (driven by smoke-free products)
- Expected U.S. nicotine pouch volume: **570-580 million cans**
- Expected operating cash flow: **~$11 billion**
- Expected effective tax rate: **21-22%**

### Effectiveness Assessment: **HIGHLY EFFECTIVE (Rating: 8.5/10)**

**Strengths:**
- Double-digit organic revenue growth (11%+) significantly outpaces reported growth
- Successful transformation to smoke-free products with strong volume growth
- Market share gains demonstrate competitive strength
- Pricing power provides margin protection against inflation
- Clear strategic focus with measurable KPIs

**Limitations/Risks:**
- Combustible cigarette volumes continue to decline (-1.4% in 2023)
- Regulatory pressures (tax increases, flavor bans, plain packaging)
- Inflationary cost pressures (~$580M impact in 2023)
- Wellness & Healthcare segment underperforming (goodwill impairment)
- Currency headwinds (Egyptian pound, Indonesian rupiah, Japanese yen, Russian ruble)

---

## Part 2: Palantir Technologies (PLTR) - Effectiveness of Founder Voting Structures in Maintaining Governance Control (as of April 2024)

### Governance Structure Overview

Palantir's founder voting structures demonstrate **exceptionally effective governance control mechanisms**, enabling founders to maintain near-majority voting control while operating as a public company:

| Share Class | Votes Per Share | Outstanding Shares (April 11, 2024) | Aggregate Votes |
|-------------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|-----------------|
| Class A Common Stock | 1 vote | 2,130,436,065 | 2,130,436,065 |
| Class B Common Stock | 10 votes | 95,553,958 | 955,539,580 |
| Class F Common Stock | ~1,040.768 votes* | 1,005,000 | 1,045,971,548 |

*Variable voting power calculated to achieve 49.999999% founder control

### Key Control Mechanisms

**1. Dual-Class Share Structure (Highly Effective)**
- Class B shares carry **10x voting power** of Class A shares
- Class F shares carry **variable super-voting rights** (~1,040 votes per share for director elections)
- Concentrates voting power with founders despite minority economic ownership

**2. Founder Voting Trust (Highly Effective)**
- All 1,005,000 Class F shares held in Founder Voting Trust
- Trustee: Wilmington Trust, National Association
- Voting instructions from founders determine Class F vote
- Decision rule: **2 of 3 founders must match** for Class F to vote

**3. Founder Voting Agreement (Highly Effective)**
- Covers all Class A and Class B shares held by founders/affiliates (except Designated Founders' Excluded Shares)
- **898,688,485 votes** subject to agreement as of April 2024
- All covered shares vote **identically** to Class F shares
- Creates unified founder voting bloc

**4. Ownership Threshold Protection (Effective)**
- Requires founders to hold **100 million Corporation Equity Securities** collectively
- Status as of April 2024: **Threshold SATISFIED**
- If not met, Class F shares would revert to 10 votes per share (vs. ~1,040)
- Provides ongoing incentive for founders to maintain significant equity stakes

**5. Board Composition Control (Effective)**
| Director | Position | Founder Status | Independence |
|----------|----------|----------------|--------------|
| Alexander Karp | CEO, Director | Co-Founder | Not Independent |
| Stephen Cohen | President, Secretary, Director | Co-Founder | Not Independent |
| Peter Thiel | Chairman, Director | Co-Founder | Not Independent |
| Alexander Moore | Director | Independent | Yes |
| Alexandra Schiff | Director | Independent | Yes |
| Lauren Friedman Stat | Director | Independent | Yes |
| Eric Woersching | Director | Independent | Yes |

- **3 of 7 board seats** held by founders (including Chairman and CEO)
- Founders control key executive positions
- Board elected annually (until Class F Conversion, then staggered 3-year terms)

### Founder Voting Power Summary (as of April 11, 2024)

| Founder | Class A Shares | Class B Shares | Class F Shares | % of Total Votes |
|---------|---------------|---------------|----------------|------------------|
| Alexander Karp | 6,432,258 | 91,725,319 | 335,000 | 11.9% |
| Stephen Cohen | 592 | 33,712,967 | 335,000 | 3.0% |
| Peter Thiel | 112,417,537 | 29,128,444 | 335,000 | 9.8% |
| **Total Founder Control** | **118,850,387** | **154,566,730** | **1,005,000** | **49.999999%** |

### Effectiveness Assessment: **EXCEPTIONALLY EFFECTIVE (Rating: 9.5/10)**

**Strengths:**
- Founders maintain **49.999999% voting control** - effectively blocking any majority-required matters
- Class F super-voting shares provide disproportionate control relative to economic ownership
- Founder Voting Trust + Agreement ensure **coordinated voting** across all founder-held shares
- Ownership threshold provides ongoing alignment incentive
- Board control with founders in CEO and Chairman positions
- Structure designed to remain in place **until Class F Conversion**

**Limitations/Risks:**
- **Concentrated control** reduces public shareholder influence on governance matters
- **Founder dependency** - company highly dependent on Alexander Karp (noted in 10-K risk factors)
- **Potential conflicts** between founder interests and public shareholders
- **DFES flexibility** - Peter Thiel's Designated Founders' Excluded Shares (121M votes) can be voted independently, potentially creating founder disagreement
- **No cumulative voting** - reduces minority shareholder ability to elect directors
- **Plurality voting** for directors - founders can elect directors without majority support

---

## Comparative Analysis

| Dimension | PM Performance Metrics | PLTR Voting Structures |
|-----------|----------------------|----------------------|
| **Primary Objective** | Drive organic revenue growth | Maintain founder governance control |
| **Effectiveness Rating** | 8.5/10 (Highly Effective) | 9.5/10 (Exceptionally Effective) |
| **Quantitative Outcome** | 11%+ organic revenue growth | 49.999999% voting control |
| **Sustainability** | Dependent on market conditions, regulatory environment | Structurally embedded until Class F Conversion |
| **Key Risk** | Regulatory pressures, combustible decline | Founder dependency, shareholder conflicts |
| **Strategic Alignment** | Aligns with smoke-free transformation strategy | Aligns with long-term founder vision |
| **Measurability** | Highly measurable (revenue, volume, share) | Highly measurable (voting percentages) |

---

## Conclusion

**Philip Morris International's 2024 performance metrics are highly effective in driving organic growth**, achieving 11%+ organic revenue growth through successful smoke-free product transformation, pricing power, and market share gains. However, effectiveness is moderated by ongoing combustible volume decline, regulatory pressures, and underperformance in the Wellness & Healthcare segment.

**Palantir Technologies' founder voting structures are exceptionally effective in maintaining governance control as of April 2024**, enabling founders to maintain 49.999999% voting control through a sophisticated multi-class share structure, Founder Voting Trust, and Founder Voting Agreement. The structure is more structurally robust than PM's performance metrics but carries governance risks related to concentrated control and founder dependency.

**Overall Assessment:** PLTR's governance control mechanisms (9.5/10) demonstrate slightly higher effectiveness than PM's organic growth metrics (8.5/10) due to the structural, legally-embedded nature of voting control versus the market-dependent nature of business performance metrics. However, both mechanisms are highly effective within their respective domains.

Compare the roles of the reporting persons, Daniel Gallagher as Chief Legal Officer and Malka Meyer as Director, in the context of their respective ownership correction filings for Robinhood Markets, Inc. (NASDAQ:HOOD) in 2022 and 2024.

# Comparison of Ownership Correction Filings: Daniel Gallagher vs. Malka Meyer for Robinhood Markets, Inc. (NASDAQ: HOOD)

## Overview

Both Daniel Gallagher (Chief Legal Officer) and Malka Meyer (Director) filed amended Forms 4/A to correct errors in their previously filed ownership reports for Robinhood Markets, Inc. Below is a detailed comparison of their respective correction filings.

---

## Daniel Gallagher — Chief Legal Officer

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| **Amendment Filing Date** | February 15, 2022 |
| **Original Filing Date** | July 30, 2021 |
| **Transaction Date** | July 28, 2021 |
| **Role** | Chief Legal Officer |
| **SEC Accession Number (Amended)** | 0001783879-22-000040 |

### Nature of the Correction

The original Form 4 incorrectly reported that **220,032 shares** of Common Stock had been withheld by Robinhood to satisfy tax withholding obligations in connection with the vesting and settlement of 487,862 Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). The amendment corrected this to **235,649 shares** — an underreporting of **15,617 shares** (approximately 7.1% higher than originally stated). The transaction was coded "F" (payment of exercise price or tax liability by delivering or withholding securities) at a price of **$38.00 per share**.

### Context of the Transaction

This correction related to the Robinhood IPO liquidity event. Gallagher's RSUs vested upon the IPO, and shares were automatically withheld to cover taxes. The original filing also reported a sale of 6,900 shares (Code S) at a weighted average price of $38.4623. Following the corrected withholding, Gallagher directly owned **252,213 shares** (down from the originally reported 267,830).

### Key Remarks
- The amendment explicitly stated: *"This amendment also serves to correct the corresponding amounts that were carried forward on subsequent Form 4 reports filed by the Reporting Person."*
- The correction cascaded through future filings, meaning multiple subsequent reports were affected by this error.

---

## Malka Meyer — Director

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| **Amendment Filing Date** | November 21, 2024 |
| **Original Filing Date** | October 10, 2024 |
| **Transaction Date** | October 8, 2024 |
| **Role** | Director |
| **SEC Accession Number (Amended)** | 0000950170-24-129704 |

### Nature of the Correction

The original Form 4 incorrectly reported that the **Malka Kleiner Revocable Trust** (the "Malka Trust") held **60,446 shares** of Class A Common Stock in Column 5 of Table I. The amendment corrected this to **2,703,641 shares** — an underreporting of **2,643,195 shares** (representing an enormous undercount; the corrected figure is approximately 44.7× the originally reported amount). The filing also reported a sale of 3,225,806 shares by affiliated funds at a weighted average price of $25.0724 (pursuant to a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan).

### Context of the Transaction

Meyer is the founder and managing partner of the Ribbit Capital family of funds, and his ownership includes shares held through multiple entities: various Ribbit Capital funds (29,357,336 shares indirectly), direct holdings (20,069 shares), the Malka Trust (2,703,641 shares after correction), and Tibbir Holdings LLC (102,183 shares). The sale of 3,225,806 shares was made pursuant to a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted by Bullfrog Capital, L.P. on May 10, 2024.

### Key Remarks
- The amendment stated: *"This amendment to the Form 4 originally filed on October 10, 2024... is being filed solely to correct the number of shares held by the Malka Trust... The error in the Original Form 4 was carried forward on a subsequent report, and all reports are deemed updated by the filing of this amendment."*
- Meyer, as trustee of the Malka Trust, disclaims beneficial ownership of the trust shares except to the extent of his pecuniary interest.

---

## Comparative Analysis

| Aspect | Daniel Gallagher | Malka Meyer |
|---|---|---|
| **Role** | Chief Legal Officer (executive officer) | Director (non-executive, affiliated with Ribbit Capital) |
| **Year of Amendment** | 2022 (covering 2021 IPO transaction) | 2024 (covering 2024 sale transaction) |
| **Type of Error** | Understated shares withheld for taxes (Code F) | Understated shares held by a trust in Column 5 |
| **Magnitude of Error** | 15,617 shares (7.1% error) | 2,643,195 shares (4,373% error) |
| **Error in** | Transaction amount (Column 4 of Table I) | Post-transaction holdings (Column 5 of Table I) |
| **Source of Error** | Miscalculation of tax withholding | Carry-forward error in trust holdings reporting |
| **Cascading Impact** | Yes — affected subsequent Form 4 filings | Yes — affected a subsequent report |
| **Nature of Holdings** | Direct ownership only (personal RSUs) | Complex indirect ownership through multiple entities and trusts |
| **Transaction Context** | IPO-related RSU vesting and tax withholding | Regular course sale under 10b5-1 plan |

## Key Differences in Roles and Context

1. **Gallagher, as Chief Legal Officer**, was an insider executive whose correction involved the mechanics of IPO-related equity compensation — specifically, the proper calculation of shares withheld for tax purposes upon RSU vesting. His holdings structure was straightforward (direct ownership of personally granted RSUs), and the error was relatively modest.

2. **Meyer, as a Director**, had a far more complex ownership structure as the founder of Ribbit Capital, with holdings spread across multiple investment funds, a revocable trust, and other entities. His correction involved a substantial misreporting of trust-held shares, likely due to a data carry-forward error that dramatically understated the Malka Trust's holdings by over 2.6 million shares.

3. **Both amendments** explicitly noted that the errors were carried forward to subsequent reports, requiring the amendments to retroactively correct not just the original filing but all downstream reports. This highlights the cascading nature of Section 16 reporting errors.

4. **Timing**: Gallagher's correction came roughly 7 months after the original filing (July 2021 → February 2022), while Meyer's correction came roughly 6 weeks after the original filing (October → November 2024).

**Answer: NO**

Builders FirstSource, Inc. (NYSE:BLDR) did **NOT** exceed the threshold Recordable Incident Rate (RIR) of 2.84 required to trigger any payment under the Safety component of the 2022 Plan.

**Explanation:**

According to the 2023 Proxy Statement (DEF 14A) filed on April 28, 2023:

1. **Threshold RIR:** The 2022 Corporate Incentive Plan set a 2.84 RIR threshold to trigger any payment under the Safety component. This was equivalent to the Company's 2021 RIR performance.

2. **Actual 2022 RIR Achieved:** The Company achieved an RIR of **2.21** in 2022, representing a 22% improvement from the prior year.

3. **Interpretation of "Exceed":** In the context of safety metrics, a **lower** RIR indicates better safety performance (fewer recordable incidents). The threshold of 2.84 means that payment is triggered when the RIR is **at or below** 2.84. 

4. **Result:** Since 2.21 is **below** 2.84 (not above/exceeding it), the Company did NOT exceed the threshold. In fact, the Company performed significantly better than the threshold, achieving not only the threshold (2.84) and target (2.56), but also the maximum payout threshold (2.30). As stated in the filing: "Each of our NEOs earned the maximum payout of 200% of the Safety metric, or 20% of total target bonus payout."

**Summary Table:**
| Metric | RIR Value |
|--------|-----------|
| Threshold (to trigger payment) | 2.84 |
| Target | 2.56 |
| Maximum (for 200% payout) | 2.30 |
| Actual 2022 Achievement | 2.21 |

What is the potential share dilution, in terms of share count, from Paramount Skydance Corporation's convertible notes outstanding on 12/31/2020?

Based on ViacomCBS's (the predecessor to Paramount Global / Paramount Skydance Corporation) 2020 10-K filing for the year ended December 31, 2020, the potential share dilution from the Mandatory Convertible Senior Notes is as follows:

**Total potential dilution: approximately 24.68 million shares of Class B common stock**

This is composed of two series of Mandatory Convertible Senior Notes, both issued on February 14, 2017:

| Series | Principal Amount | Conversion Rate (per $50 principal) | Conversion Price | Shares Upon Conversion |
|--------|-----------------|-------------------------------------|------------------|------------------------|
| 5.75% Senior Notes due 2031 | $1.0 billion | 0.6415 shares | ~$77.94 | **12.83 million** |
| 6.25% Senior Notes due 2032 | $985 million | 0.6016 shares | ~$83.11 | **11.85 million** |
| **Total** | **$1.985 billion** | | | **~24.68 million** |

**Calculation details:**
- 5.75% Notes: ($1,000,000,000 ÷ $50) × 0.6415 = 20,000,000 × 0.6415 = 12,830,000 shares
- 6.25% Notes: ($985,000,000 ÷ $50) × 0.6016 = 19,700,000 × 0.6016 = 11,851,520 shares
- Total: 12,830,000 + 11,851,520 = **24,681,520 shares**

The filing itself states approximately 12.8 million shares for the 5.75% notes and approximately 11.9 million shares for the 6.25% notes, totaling approximately 24.7 million shares. Using the adjusted conversion rates reported in the diluted EPS footnote (0.6421 and 0.6022 respectively for 2020), the total would be approximately 24,705,340 shares.

The conversion rates are subject to anti-dilution adjustments, which explain the slight differences between the stated rates.

How did the treatment of Restructuring and other charges differ between the Arconic Inc. (NYSE:ARNC) 2018 filing and the Howmet Aerospace Inc. (NYSE:HWM) 2020 filing in the reconciliation to Income from continuing operations?

## Comparison of Restructuring and Other Charges Treatment

### Arconic Inc. (NYSE: ARNC) 2018 Filing
**Filing:** 2018 10-K (filed February 21, 2019, report date December 31, 2018)

**Reconciliation Direction:** Top-down (from Total segment operating profit DOWN to Consolidated income from continuing operations before income taxes)

**Treatment of Restructuring and other charges:**
- **2018 Amount:** $(9) million
- **Presentation:** Shown as **negative values** (in parentheses) under "Unallocated amounts"
- **Position in reconciliation:** Deducted from Total segment operating profit along with Corporate expense (and Impairment of goodwill when applicable) to arrive at Consolidated operating income. Then Interest expense and Other (expense) income, net are deducted to arrive at Consolidated income from continuing operations before income taxes.

**Reconciliation Table Structure:**
```
Total segment operating profit                    $ 1,581
Unallocated amounts:
  Impairment of goodwill                          —
  Restructuring and other charges                 (9)
  Corporate expense                               (247)
Consolidated operating income                     $ 1,325
Interest expense                                  (378)
Other (expense) income, net                       (79)
Consolidated income from continuing operations 
  before income taxes                             $ 868
```

---

### Howmet Aerospace Inc. (NYSE: HWM) 2020 Filing
**Filing:** 2020 10-K (filed February 16, 2021, report date December 31, 2020)

**Reconciliation Direction:** Bottom-up (from Income from continuing operations before income taxes UP to Total segment operating profit)

**Treatment of Restructuring and other charges:**
- **2020 Amount:** $182 million
- **Presentation:** Shown as **positive values** under "Unallocated amounts"
- **Position in reconciliation:** Interest expense and Other expense (income), net are added first to Income from continuing operations before income taxes to arrive at Consolidated operating income. Then Restructuring and other charges and Corporate expense are added to arrive at Total segment operating profit.

**Reconciliation Table Structure:**
```
Income from continuing operations before income taxes  $ 171
Interest expense                                        381
Other expense (income), net                              74
Consolidated operating income                          $ 626
Unallocated amounts:
  Restructuring and other charges                       182
  Corporate expense                                      82
Total segment operating profit                         $ 890
```

---

### Key Differences

1. **Direction of Reconciliation:**
   - **Arconic 2018:** Reconciles FROM Total segment operating profit TO Income from continuing operations (top-down)
   - **Howmet 2020:** Reconciles FROM Income from continuing operations TO Total segment operating profit (bottom-up)

2. **Sign Convention:**
   - **Arconic 2018:** Restructuring and other charges shown as **negative values** (deductions)
   - **Howmet 2020:** Restructuring and other charges shown as **positive values** (add-backs)

3. **Position Relative to Other Line Items:**
   - **Arconic 2018:** Restructuring charges are deducted **before** arriving at Consolidated operating income; Interest and Other items are deducted **after** to reach Income from continuing operations
   - **Howmet 2020:** Interest and Other items are added **first** to reach Consolidated operating income; Restructuring charges are added **after** to reach Total segment operating profit

**Note:** Despite these presentational differences, the underlying economic treatment is consistent—Restructuring and other charges are classified as "Unallocated amounts" that reduce operating income relative to segment operating profit in both filings.

By April 7, 2023, what is the total dollar value (in thousands) of Cognizant's operating leases that will mature within the next three years, and what proportion does this represent?

Based on Cognizant's 10-K filing for the year ended December 31, 2022 (filed February 15, 2023), which is the most recent filing available by April 7, 2023:

**Operating Lease Maturity Schedule (in millions):**
- 2023: $215 million
- 2024: $180 million
- 2025: $155 million
- 2026: $129 million
- 2027: $108 million
- Thereafter: $267 million
- **Total operating lease payments: $1,054 million**
- Less: Imputed interest: $166 million
- **Total operating lease liabilities: $888 million**

**Calculation:**
- Total dollar value of operating leases maturing within the next three years (2023, 2024, 2025): $215 + $180 + $155 = $550 million
- In thousands: $550,000 thousand

**Proportion:**
- Proportion of total operating lease payments: $550 / $1,054 = 0.5218 = **52.18%**

**Answer:**
- Total dollar value (in thousands): **$550,000**

## Arch Capital Group's Stock-based Compensation Adjustment in 2021

After reviewing Arch Capital Group Ltd.'s (ACGL) 2021 10-K filing (filed February 25, 2022), I found that the most directly relevant "adjustment" to stock-based compensation expense appears in the **income tax reconciliation** (Note 15 – Income Taxes).

### Income Tax Reconciliation Adjustment

In the reconciliation of expected income tax expense to actual income tax expense, Arch Capital reported a **"Share based compensation" adjustment of $(5,339) thousand**, or **$(5.34) million** for 2021. This represents an excess tax benefit (a reduction in the income tax provision) arising from stock-based compensation — typically when the market price of shares at exercise/vesting exceeds the grant-date fair value, creating a larger tax deduction than the compensation expense recognized for book purposes.

For comparison:
- 2021: $(5,339) thousand
- 2020: $(2,533) thousand
- 2019: $(6,592) thousand

### Total Stock-Based Compensation Expense (for context)

The total pre-tax stock-based compensation expense recognized for 2021 was **$86,580 thousand** ($86.58 million), as reported in Note 22 – Share-Based Compensation:

| **Total** | **$86,580K** |

This compares to $69,892K in 2020 and $63,848K in 2019.

### Conclusion

Based on the filings, **Arch Capital Group adjusted its stock-based compensation by $(5.34) million** in the income tax reconciliation for 2021. There was no explicit modification, true-up, forfeiture rate change, or other direct adjustment to the stock-based compensation expense itself disclosed in the 2021 10-K beyond the normal performance award true-up mechanism embedded in the accounting for performance-based awards.

## Incyte Q3 2023 GAAP Gross Margin: Actual vs. Forecast

### Guidance/Forecast
Incyte provided its **full year 2023 GAAP gross margin guidance** in its Q2 2023 earnings press release (issued August 1, 2023) of **93.0% to 93.5%**. This was the first time the company provided GAAP gross margin guidance (previously listed as "not previously provided"). The midpoint of this range is **93.25%**.

### Actual Q3 2023 GAAP Gross Margin
From the Q3 2023 10-Q (filed October 31, 2023), the actual Q3 2023 results were:

| Item | Amount ($ thousands) |
|------|---------------------|
| Total Revenues | $919,025 |
| Cost of Product Revenues | $60,091 |
| Gross Profit | $858,934 |

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Actual Q3 2023 GAAP Gross Margin | 93.46% |
| FY 2023 Guidance Midpoint | 93.25% |
| **Difference** | **+0.21 percentage points** |

For reference:
- Versus the low end (93.0%): exceeded by ~46 bps
- Versus the high end (93.5%): fell short by ~4 bps

### Calculation
- Actual GAAP gross margin: $858,934 / $919,025 = 93.4607%
- Guidance midpoint: (93.0% + 93.5%) / 2 = 93.25%
- Difference: 93.46% - 93.25% = +0.21 percentage points = **+21 basis points**

Compute the 2‑year revenue CAGR for Verisk Analytics between 2020 and 2022.

## 2-Year Revenue CAGR for Verisk Analytics (2020-2022)

### Calculation

To compute the 2-year Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR), I used the formula:

**CAGR = (Ending Value / Beginning Value)^(1/n) - 1**

Where:
- Ending Value = 2022 Revenue
- Beginning Value = 2020 Revenue
- n = 2 years

### Revenue Figures

I retrieved revenue data from Verisk Analytics' SEC 10-K filings. A critical finding was that Verisk classified its Energy business as a **discontinued operation** in Q4 2022. Per the 2022 10-K, all results of the Energy business were removed from continuing operations and presented as discontinued operations for **all periods presented** (2020, 2021, and 2022).

For a proper CAGR calculation, I used the **restated continuing operations revenue figures** from the 2022 10-K to ensure comparability across all years:

- **2020 Revenue (restated, continuing operations):** $2,269.4 million
- **2022 Revenue (continuing operations):** $2,497.0 million

### CAGR Calculation

```
CAGR = (2,497.0 / 2,269.4)^(1/2) - 1
     = (1.1002908258)^(0.5) - 1
     = 1.0489474853 - 1
     = 0.0489474853
     = 4.89474853%
```

**2-Year Revenue CAGR (2020-2022) = 4.89%**

### Note on Restated Figures

The 2020 10-K originally reported 2020 revenue as $2,784.6 million (including the Energy business). However, the 2022 10-K restated this to $2,269.4 million (excluding the Energy business, which had $515.2 million in 2020 revenue). Using restated figures ensures the CAGR reflects growth of the comparable continuing business.

Did Domino's achieve its Q4 FY 2020 pre‑tax margin goal, and if not, by how many basis points did it miss?

## Domino's Q4 FY2020 Pre-Tax Margin Goal Analysis

### The Goal
Domino's long-standing 2-to-3 year outlook, presented at its 2018 Investor Day, included a target of achieving a pre-tax margin of approximately **16%** (with the target timeframe spanning fiscal years 2019-2021).

### Q4 FY2020 Actual Performance

To calculate Domino's Q4 FY2020 pre-tax margin, I derived the quarterly figures from their SEC filings:

| Period | Income Before Taxes | Total Revenues | Pre-Tax Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 2020 | $117.296M | $873.102M | 13.43% |
| Q2 2020 | $124.496M | $920.023M | 13.53% |
| Q3 2020 | $123.773M | $967.719M | 12.79% |
| **9-Months 2020** | **$365.565M** | **$2,760.844M** | **13.24%** |
| **FY2020 (Full Year)** | **$555.1M** | **$4,117.4M** | **13.48%** |

**Q4 FY2020 (derived as FY2020 minus 9-month):**
- Income Before Taxes: $555.1M − $365.565M = **$189.535M**
- Total Revenues: $4,117.4M − $2,760.844M = **$1,356.556M**
- Q4 FY2020 Pre-Tax Margin: **$189.535M / $1,356.556M = 13.97%**

### The Verdict
**No, Domino's did not achieve its pre-tax margin goal in Q4 FY2020.** The company fell short of its approximately 16% pre-tax margin target by approximately **203 basis points** (16.00% − 13.97% = 2.03 percentage points, or 203 bps).

- Domino's FY2020 10-K (filed Feb 25, 2021): Full year income before taxes ($555.1M) and revenues ($4,117.4M)

- Domino's Q2 FY2020 10-Q (filed Jul 16, 2020): Q2 income before taxes and revenues

What were the specific customer base adjustments made by T-Mobile US, Inc. (NASDAQ:TMUS) in fiscal year 2020 to align Sprint policies, how did the April 1, 2020 Stockholders' Agreement adjust voting rights for Deutsche Telekom AG, and what exclusions were applied to accounts receivable in the April 30, 2020 EIP Receivables Facility amendment?

## T-Mobile US, Inc. (TMUS) – Fiscal Year 2020 Specific Disclosures

---

### 1. Customer Base Adjustments to Align Sprint Policies

In connection with the April 1, 2020 merger with Sprint, T-Mobile made the following **seven specific customer base adjustments** as of March 31, 2020 (the "beginning customers" as of April 1, 2020), to align Sprint's customer reporting policies with T-Mobile's policies. The total adjustment removed **14,060,000 customers** from the combined base:

| # | Adjustment Category | Impact (000s) | Description |
|---|-------------------|---------------|-------------|
| (1) | **Reseller reclassification to wholesale** | (3,071) | Refined definition of wholesale customers — certain postpaid and prepaid reseller customers reclassified to wholesale. T-Mobile discontinued reporting wholesale customer counts, focusing instead on postpaid/prepaid customers and wholesale revenues. |
| (2) | **EIP reclassification from postpaid to prepaid** | Net 0 (963 moved) | Prepaid customers with a device installment billing plan historically included as Sprint postpaid customers were reclassified to prepaid to align with T-Mobile policy. (963K from postpaid phone → prepaid) |
| (3) | **Divested prepaid customers** | (9,207) | Customers associated with the Sprint wireless prepaid and Boost Mobile brands (divested on July 1, 2020 per DOJ consent decree) were excluded from reported customers. |
| (4) | **Rate plan threshold** | (1,100) | Customers with rate plans having monthly recurring charges considered "insignificant" were excluded from reported customers. |
| (5) | **Non-phone device reclassification** | Net 0 (226 moved) | Customers with postpaid phone rate plans but without a phone (e.g., non-phone devices like tablets, hotspots) were reclassified from postpaid phone to postpaid other customers. |
| (6) | **Collection policy alignment** | (196) | Certain Sprint customers subject to collection activity for an extended period of time were excluded from reported customers to align with T-Mobile's more conservative collection/write-off policy. |
| (7) | **Miscellaneous adjustments** | (486) | Miscellaneous insignificant adjustments to align with T-Mobile policy. |

The adjustments were distributed across customer types as follows:
- **Postpaid phone**: (1,861,000) reduction
- **Postpaid other**: (3,653,000) reduction
- **Prepaid**: (8,546,000) reduction
- **Total**: (14,060,000) reduction, bringing combined customers from 111,143,000 to 97,083,000

---

### 2. April 1, 2020 Stockholders' Agreement — Voting Rights Adjustments for Deutsche Telekom AG

On April 1, 2020, in connection with the Sprint merger closing, T-Mobile, Deutsche Telekom AG ("DT"), and SoftBank Group Corp. entered into two key agreements that fundamentally adjusted DT's voting control:

#### Amended and Restated Stockholders' Agreement
- **Board designation rights**: DT received the right to designate **9 out of 14** board nominees (SoftBank: 4 nominees, with the 14th director being the CEO).
- **Consent/veto rights (30% ownership threshold)**: As long as DT beneficially owns ≥30% of outstanding T-Mobile voting securities, T-Mobile cannot take certain actions without DT's prior written consent, including: (a) incurring indebtedness above a specified debt-to-cash-flow ratio, (b) actions causing default under DT or its affiliates' debt, (c) acquisitions/disposals/mergers exceeding $1.0 billion, (d) changing Board size, (e) issuing equity ≥10% of outstanding shares (with exceptions), (f) share repurchases or extraordinary/non-pro-rata dividends, and (g) certain changes involving the CEO.
- **Ownership cap**: DT is restricted from acquiring more than 80.1% of T-Mobile voting securities.

#### Proxy, Lock-up and ROFR Agreement (the "Proxy Agreement")
- **Proxy voting mechanism**: At any stockholder meeting, **SoftBank's shares (~24% of outstanding T-Mobile common stock) must be voted in the manner directed by Deutsche Telekom**. This Proxy effectively gives DT voting control over SoftBank's entire stake.
- **Termination triggers**: The Proxy obligation terminates upon the earliest of: (i) SoftBank transferring shares to a third party, (ii) DT owning ≥55% of outstanding T-Mobile voting securities, or (iii) DT transferring shares representing ≥5% of outstanding T-Mobile common stock (as measured at closing).
- **Mutual transfer restrictions**: Both DT and SoftBank are restricted from transferring their shares without the other's consent until the 4th anniversary of closing, subject to exceptions (up to 5% after year 1, and an additional 10% after year 2).
- **Controlled company status**: As a result of the Proxy Agreement, **T-Mobile continued to be a "controlled company" under NASDAQ rules**, exempting it from certain corporate governance requirements (e.g., independent director majority, independent compensation committee).

Post-closing ownership: DT held ~43% and SoftBank held ~24% of outstanding T-Mobile common stock. With the Proxy, DT effectively controlled approximately **67%** of the voting power.

---

### 3. April 30, 2020 EIP Receivables Facility Amendment — Accounts Receivable Exclusions

On April 30, 2020, T-Mobile entered into the **Third Amendment** to the Third Amended and Restated Receivables Purchase and Administration Agreement (the "EIP Receivables Facility"), among T-Mobile Handset Funding LLC (transferor), T-Mobile Financial LLC (servicer), T-Mobile US, Inc. and T-Mobile USA, Inc. (guarantors), Royal Bank of Canada (Administrative Agent), and various funding agents.

The EIP Receivables Facility had a maximum funding commitment of **$1.3 billion** and involved the sale of certain Equipment Installment Plan (EIP) accounts receivable on a revolving basis.

The Third Amendment provided the following, for a period of **up to 7 months**:

1. **Flexibility for modifications to accounts receivable sold** — T-Mobile's collection policies were updated to temporarily allow for flexibility for modifications to the accounts receivable sold in the facility that were **impacted by COVID-19** (e.g., payment deferrals, extended payment terms).

2. **Exclusion from pool performance triggers** — The COVID-19-impacted accounts receivable were **excluded from all pool performance triggers**. This meant that any deterioration in the performance (delinquencies, defaults, etc.) of these specifically identified COVID-19-impacted receivables would not count against the facility's performance metrics or trigger any early amortization, termination, or other adverse events under the facility.

In summary, the exclusions insulated the facility's performance metrics from the effects of COVID-19-related customer accommodations, protecting T-Mobile's access to this $1.3 billion funding source during the pandemic.
